name: Artemis
kicker: Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon · Twin sister of Apollo
dates: Honored across ancient Greece for well over 1,000 years
briefing: Artemis grew up fast: legend says she helped deliver her own twin brother, Apollo, just moments after she herself was born on the island of Delos. As goddess of the hunt and the moon, she roamed the wilderness with a silver bow and a pack of hounds, and she had a fierce, no-exceptions rule — anyone who disrespected her paid for it, like the hunter Actaeon, whom she turned into a stag for spying on her.

qb.tip: Only 3 came back at Middle School/Easy High School, so a difficulties=3 (Regular HS) search filled out the sample. Unlike Poseidon’s “no Neptune” rule, most sets here DO accept “Diana,” sometimes only until the word “Greek” is read.

sample.note: 7 real QBReader tossups (3 Middle School/Easy High School + 4 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: As a child, this goddess asked her father, Zeus, for a bow and arrows, a pack of hunting dogs, and eternal companions, a band of nymphs. Homer calls this goddess “Potnia Theron” [“POT-nee-uh THEH-ron”], or “Mistress of the Animals.” She is credited with placing the hunter Orion among the stars as a constellation.
tossups.r: This goddess turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag after he saw her bathing. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, the twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: Along with Athena and Hestia, this goddess is one of three Olympians who never married. She is considered a protector of wild animals and young girls as well as a goddess of the hunt. Out of pity, this goddess once turned the grieving sisters of the hero Meleager into guinea hens.
tossups.r: When King Oeneus forgot to honor her with a sacrifice, this goddess sent the Calydonian Boar to ravage his kingdom of Aetolia. For 10 points, name this twin sister of Apollo, the Greek goddess of the hunt.

tossups.p: Some myths say this goddess was born a day before her twin brother, on the island of Ortygia, an old name for Delos. After a woman named Chione bragged that she was prettier than her, this goddess shot Chione with an arrow.
tossups.r: Because this goddess was angry with Agamemnon, the Greek fleet was becalmed at Aulis until he agreed to sacrifice his daughter Iphigenia. For 10 points, name this goddess who turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag, the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: This goddess tricked the giant twins Otus and Ephialtes [“eh-fee-AL-teez”] into killing each other, in some versions by transforming into a deer and running between them. When Niobe boasted that she had more children than Leto, this goddess killed Niobe’s daughters while her brother killed the sons.
tossups.r: This goddess’s temple at Ephesus was counted as one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: Moments after her own birth, this goddess is said to have helped her mother, Leto, deliver her twin brother, which is why she is linked to childbirth. This goddess once sent a she-bear to nurse the infant Atalanta after Atalanta’s father abandoned her on a mountainside.
tossups.r: This goddess turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag after he stumbled upon her bathing. For 10 points, name this twin sister of Apollo, the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: This goddess carries the epithet “Potnia Theron,” meaning “Mistress of the Animals.” She placed the hunter Orion, whom she admired, among the stars as a constellation after his death. She is a protector of wild creatures and of young girls approaching adulthood.
tossups.r: This goddess tricked the giants Otus and Ephialtes into killing each other by running between them in the form of a deer. For 10 points, name this eternally virgin Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: This goddess sent a monstrous boar to destroy the region of Aetolia after King Oeneus neglected to sacrifice to her. She later took pity on the Meleagrids, sisters of the hero who killed that boar, and turned them into guinea hens.
tossups.r: This goddess becalmed the Greek fleet at Aulis, forcing Agamemnon to sacrifice his daughter Iphigenia to her. For 10 points, name this twin sister of Apollo, the Greek goddess of the hunt.

tossups.p: This goddess is one of three eternally unmarried Olympian goddesses, alongside Athena and Hestia. As a little girl, she is said to have asked Zeus for hunting dogs, a silver bow, and nymphs to keep her company forever.
tossups.r: After Niobe boasted of having more children than Leto, this goddess killed Niobe’s daughters while her twin brother killed the sons. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: This goddess may have been born on the island of Ortygia a day before her more famous twin brother. She is considered a protector of wild creatures and of young girls approaching adulthood, as well as a goddess of the hunt.
tossups.r: She turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag for the crime of seeing her bathe. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, the twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: After a woman named Chione claimed to be more beautiful than her, this goddess shot and killed her with an arrow. A temple to this goddess at Ephesus was counted among the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
tossups.r: This goddess once tricked two giant brothers, Otus and Ephialtes, into killing each other with javelins. For 10 points, name this eternally virgin Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: This goddess sent a she-bear to nurse the abandoned infant Atalanta, who grew up to become a great huntress herself. Homer calls this goddess “Mistress of the Animals,” and she is said to have asked Zeus for her silver bow as a small child.
tossups.r: This goddess sent the Calydonian Boar to ravage Aetolia after King Oeneus forgot to honor her at a festival. For 10 points, name this twin sister of Apollo, the Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: This goddess is said to have placed the hunter Orion among the stars as a constellation. Along with her twin brother, this goddess killed all of Niobe’s children after Niobe boasted about having more of them than their mother, Leto.
tossups.r: This goddess’s anger becalmed the Greek fleet at Aulis until Agamemnon agreed to sacrifice his daughter Iphigenia. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon.

tossups.p: Born on Delos, this goddess is said to have helped deliver her own twin brother moments after her own birth. She is one of three Olympian goddesses, with Athena and Hestia, who chose to remain unmarried forever.
tossups.r: She turned the hunter Actaeon into a stag after he spied on her while she bathed. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, the twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: This goddess turned the grieving sisters of the hero Meleager into guinea hens and carried them off to the island of Leros. Her temple at Ephesus, rebuilt many times over the centuries, became one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
tossups.r: She once tricked the giant twins Otus and Ephialtes into killing one another. For 10 points, name this eternally virgin Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, twin sister of Apollo.

tossups.p: As a young girl, this goddess asked her father for a silver bow, hunting dogs, and a band of nymphs as lifelong companions. She later killed a boastful woman named Chione with an arrow for claiming to be prettier than her.
tossups.r: This goddess helped kill all of Niobe’s children, sparing none, after Niobe insulted her mother, Leto. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the hunt and the moon, twin sister of Apollo.

trap.title: Diana, but watch the timing
trap.body: Artemis is the Greek goddess; Diana is her Roman counterpart. Unlike Neptune for Poseidon, many tournaments DO accept “Diana” — though some only until the question says the word “Greek,” after which only “Artemis” counts. She is also one of three eternally virgin Olympians, along with Athena and Hestia, so a clue about refusing marriage alone isn’t enough to buzz.
trap.fix: “Diana” is usually safe early on, but once you hear “Greek goddess,” switch your answer to “Artemis.” And wait for a clue specific to the hunt, the moon, or her twin brother Apollo before buzzing on the virgin-goddess theme alone — it could be Athena or Hestia instead.
trap.line: Real answer line: Artemis (accept Diana, sometimes only before “Greek” is read).
